column1: # Targets of the function-pointer dispatch sites on the aarch64 interrupt
# path. Mirrors tools/irq-edges-x86_64.tsv; see that file for the rationale
# (the walker follows direct call edges only, so it stops dead at every
# `blr` unless the target is named here).
# `oxide_irq_dispatch`) is the SINGLE root that reaches every hardware
# handler indirectly. Unlike x86 there is no separate MSI-vector-table
# `tick_poll` are all small enough to have been inlined into
# `oxide_arm_irq_dispatch` in this release build (confirmed: it disassembles
# with 17 `blr` sites), so every target below is attributed directly to it
# rather than to the small wrapper fns that source-level own each table.
# Four parallel tables feed those 17 sites:
#   ARM_MSI_HANDS       (fn())      — PCI MSI/MSI-X + GICv3 LPI, `request via
#                                      is itself inlined into the dispatcher.
# Format: `<caller>\t<callee>`, demangled identities, caller repeated per
# target. An entry that no longer resolves FAILS the gate.
# NAPI poll list, one level BELOW the softirq table: `net_rx_action` walks the
# inlined into it, so the edge is attributed to `net_rx_action` itself, same
# x86 targets with NO aarch64 counterpart (omitted, not stubbed):
#   drv_ps2_keyboard::imp::irq::irq1_handler  — PS/2 is x86-only; QEMU virt
#     has no i8042. `drv-ps2-keyboard` is not in the aarch64 driver set.
#     uses `drv-uart-pl011` (`rx_isr_irq` above), a fixed-INTID line handler
#     rather than an MSI vector, so it goes through a different table
